newsitem.title: GERMANY: METRO HOLDING PROFITS UP, ON ACQUISITION TRAIL.
newsitem.headline: METRO HOLDING PROFITS UP, ON ACQUISITION TRAIL.

text.p: Swiss-based Metro Holding AG, Europe's largest diversified retail concern, on Monday announced higher 1996 profits and said talks on buying a Dutch cash-and-carry chain were progressing.
Metro Holding, parent of listed German retail group Metro AG, said group net profits rose to 992 million marks in 1996 from 853 million marks.
Group sales, net of value-added tax, rose to 67.8 billion marks from 66.7 billion marks, chief executive Erwin Conradi told a news conference here.

Metro Holding, which is privately controlled, published consolidated results for only the second time. Under a complex holding structure it controls 65.6 percent of the voting stock of Metro AG, which was created out of a merger a year ago.
Conradi told reporters Metro Holding's return on equity was 11 percent last year, a figure which he expected to rise once the synergy effects of the Metro AG fusion.
"We should seek a return on equity of 12 to 15 percent -- but the (operating) company is just a year old," he said. "We are not doing badly considering the difficult operating environment."
Through its stake in Metro AG, Metro Holding controls the Kaufhof department store chain, MediaMarkt electrical goods stores and Vobis computer outlets, among others.
Metro Holding also directly controls cash-and-carry businesses in Denmark, Austria, Italy, France, Hungary, Turkey and the U.S.
Conradi said talks were continuing with privately-owned Dutch retail group SVH Holding NV to take over its Makro cash-and-carry chain and liquidate a series of cross-holdings between the two groups.

Metro Holding already owns stakes of up to 40 percent in Makro units in the Netherlands, Belgium, Spain, Portugal, Greece, Poland, the Czech Republic and Morocco. Sales in those countries are expected to top 16 billion marks this year.
Metro Holding also wants to buy out Makro's stakes of up to 40 percent in its own cash-and-carry operations abroad.
"The talks are continuing," Conradi said. "I don't expect them to reach a 'hot phase' before mid- to late October, and then it will become clear whether and how things work out."
Conradi declined to give any details, saying: "We are talking about a big and complex deal with a limitless range of possible outcomes."
Commenting on group strategy, Conradi said the top priority was to complete the merger of Metro AG at operational level to boost the bottom line by 400 million marks a year from 1999.

He said that, with retail demand sluggish in major European markets like Germany, Metro Holding should internationalise its portfolio by using its cash-and-carry infrastructure to reduce startup costs.
He identified countries like Poland, Turkey and China as key growth markets in which Metro has already won a foothold.
Metro AG shares fell 85 pfennigs to close at 92.15 marks in late trading on the Frankfurt stock exchange.
